article_content: Newly released footage from GoPro cameras has offered an intimate, heart-pounding look at Felix Baumgartner’s historic 2012 stratospheric jump — the first time a human broke the sound barrier in freefall. Rising to 128,100 feet above the New Mexico desert in a pressurized capsule, Baumgartner spent two and a half hours ascending before plummeting back to Earth. For the first 34 seconds, he accelerated uncontrollably, eventually hitting a peak speed of 833.9 mph — Mach 1.24 — before stabilizing and deploying his parachute. During a violent, uncontrolled spin that lasted nearly 20 seconds, mission control lost contact, fearing the worst. Baumgartner later admitted he feared losing his record more than his life in those terrifying moments, though he was fully aware of the risk. The descent, captured by five cameras mounted on his suit, revealed not only the physics of supersonic freefall but also the raw human experience: isolation, disorientation, and sheer willpower. After landing safely on his feet, Baumgartner reflected not on the records broken, but on the profound humility of standing on the edge of space. 'You don’t think about medals or data up there,' he said. 'You just want to make it home.' The mission, sponsored by Red Bull, delivered groundbreaking physiological insights — the first-ever data on how the human body responds to supersonic freefall — paving the way for future aerospace safety research.

Basınlı bir kapsülde New Mexico çölünün üzerinde 128.100 ayak yüksekliğe çıkan Baumgartner, yere inmek için iki buçuk saatlik bir yükselişin ardından düşmeye başladı. article_content: More than a week after a brutal attack on buses in Iguala, southern Mexico, the search for 43 missing students continues amid horrifying discoveries. On September 26, armed men ambushed multiple vehicles carrying students from the Ayotzinapa rural teachers’ college and members of the Chilpancingo Hornets youth soccer team. Six people were killed that night, including a 15-year-old soccer player. The students—mostly young men in their early twenties—were traveling when their buses were intercepted. Authorities now believe the criminal group Guerreros Unidos, with ties to local police, orchestrated the violence. Following tips from arrested suspects, investigators uncovered several unmarked graves along a remote dirt road in Guerrero state. Inside, they found the charred remains of at least 28 individuals, burned and buried hastily. Identification could take weeks to months. The Mexican government has offered a reward of one million pesos—about $74,000—for information leading to the missing students. Over 30 people have been detained, including 22 police officers, though officials claim the officers did not initiate the attacks. Yet survivors and protesters say otherwise: eyewitnesses describe police actively directing gunfire and threatening to kill everyone on board. One soccer teammate recounted how gunmen ordered passengers to open the bus doors, shouting, 'Now you’re going to be taken—we’re going to kill all of you.' When the teacher refused, the shooting resumed. Amid national outcry, Governor Angel Aguirre expressed condolences but warned against politicizing the tragedy. Meanwhile, social media campaigns scream: 'It’s more dangerous to be a student than a criminal.' For years, Guerrero has been one of Mexico’s most violent states, where kidnappings and mass graves are tragically common—but few cases ever see justice.

article_content: This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Sophia Strother, a 43-year-old founder of L2E Industries, a multimillion-dollar delivery company based in Austin, Texas. The revenue generated by her business has been verified by Insider. The following has been edited for length and clarity. In 2018, I was reading a magazine when I came across an article about Amazon. The piece criticized the company for not partnering with small businesses to handle its deliveries. It stated that for $10,000, anyone could join Amazon’s delivery program and potentially earn between $74,000 and $3 million annually. At the time, I was a 38-year-old single mother and survivor of sex trafficking living in the Austin, Texas area. My grandmother deeply believed in me and helped me develop strong business acumen. Although I became a mother at 15, I still earned my bachelor’s and master’s degrees in business administration. At age 20, I launched my first business, Trustworthy Consulting. By the time I graduated, I owned two homes and held two degrees. As I read the Amazon article, I thought: Why not me? I applied for the partnership. Within a year, I was running a million-dollar business. After 18 months, my delivery company had grown into a multimillion-dollar enterprise. I submitted an online application, a resume, and financial documents. Amazon conducted a background check. Though I had no transportation background, I emphasized the leadership initiatives I’d led and my passion for serving families in my community. In 2019, Amazon invited me to Seattle for an interview—but I had to cover all travel costs myself. With no savings and no babysitter, and only a week to decide, I declined. I didn’t believe I could do it. That same year, the day after Christmas, I received an email from Amazon asking, 'Are you still interested?' This time, I knew I’d regret it if I didn’t seize the chance. I traveled to Las Vegas for the Amazon event, where over 200 candidates were interviewed by Amazon executives. I remember one interviewer asked, 'Will you work every day?' I replied, 'No, ma’am—I believe in work-life balance.' Two days later, I received a call offering me the partnership. We signed a formal contract for the Austin, Texas region in July 2020. I launched my first delivery route on September 22, 2020. Today, I own L2E Industries—short for Learning 2 Exhale Industries—with Amazon as my primary transportation client. We’ve generated over $3 million in revenue in under three years. I now operate a fleet of 38 blue vans marked with 'Prime,' and employ nearly 80 associates. My team picks up packages from Amazon delivery stations and delivers them to customers’ doors—or businesses—hopefully with a smile. I’m responsible for servicing part of Central Texas, managing 25 to 35 daily routes. I ensure vans are maintained and staff are prepared. On the backend, I oversee operations, planning routes tailored to rural, urban, and underserved areas. Our goal is to maximize safety and quality to drive revenue. We’re paid per package delivered and rewarded for positive customer feedback. After each delivery, customers receive a message inviting them to rate the experience: Was the delivery on time? Were drivers courteous? Did they go above and beyond? I encourage everyone to respond. Our compensation is tied to customer satisfaction, delivery quality, and consistency. But I don’t directly control business growth—Amazon does. They determine how much work I receive based on regional demand. I can’t predict we’ll average 40 routes daily in 2024. But I can commit to reinvesting a portion of profits into building other ventures. Fostering a positive company culture helps employees stay through tough times—which is exactly what happened. In February 2021, a deadly winter storm shut down operations for a week. The next quarter was devastating. I had to cash out my retirement and personal savings—and stop paying myself—to keep paying my team. Eventually, I met with an Amazon-provided business coach for 15 minutes. She analyzed performance metrics and identified underperforming staff dragging down the business. From that moment, I learned to balance compassion with accountability. I set clear deadlines for improvement and introduced standardized scorecards to evaluate driver performance. I also began making smarter financial decisions to ensure long-term sustainability. Since then, I’ve never missed a payroll and have resumed paying myself. When I worked for others, I often wished someone cared about my well-being. Now, I strive to offer that same care to my team. I’m driven not just by profit, but by the families connected to this business.

İşletmesinin geliri Insider tarafından doğrulanmıştır. Aşağıdaki metin uzunluk ve netlik açısından düzenlenmiştir. 2018'de bir dergi okurken Amazon hakkında bir makale okudum. Şirket, küçük işletmelerle kargo işbirliği yapmaması nedeniyle eleştiriliyordu. Makalede, 10.000 dolarla herkes Amazon'un kargo programına katılabilir ve yılda 74.000 ila 3 milyon dolar arasında kazanabilir deniyordu. O zamanlar, Austin, Texas bölgesinde yaşayan 38 yaşındaki tek anne ve cinsel ticaret mağduru idim. Grandam benimle çok inançlıydı ve bana ticari zeka kazandırmada yardımcı oldu. 15 yaşında bir annem olmama rağmen, lisans ve yüksek lisans derecelerimi işletme yönetimi alanında tamamladım. 20 yaşında ilk işim olan Trustworthy Consulting'i başlattım. Mezun olduğumda iki evim ve iki derecem vardı. Amazon makalesini okurken, 'Neden ben değilim?' diye düşündüm. Ortaklık için başvurdum. Bir yıl içinde milyon dolarlık bir işe sahip oldum. 18 ay sonra kargo şirketim çok milyon dolarlık bir işletmeye dönüştü. Çevrimiçi bir başvuru, bir özgeçmiş ve bazı finansal belgeler gönderdim. Amazon bir arka plan denetimi yaptı. Taşımacılık deneyimim yoktu, ancak başvuruda liderlik projelerimi ve topluluğumdaki ailelere hizmet etme tutkumu vurguladım. 2019'da Amazon, ortaklık için Seattle'a gelmemi istedi—ancak seyahat masraflarını kendim ödemek zorundaydım. Hem para hem de çocuk bakıcım yoktu ve sadece bir haftam vardı. Kabul etmedim. Bunu başarabileceğimi düşünmüyordum. Aynı yıl, Noel'den sonraki gün Amazon'dan bir e-posta aldım: 'Hâlâ bu fırsatla ilgileniyor musun?' Bu sefer, fırsatı kaçırsam pişman olacağımı biliyordum. Amazon etkinliği için Las Vegas'a gittim ve odada 200'den fazla aday vardı. Her aday, Amazon yöneticilerinden biriyle görüşmeye tabi tutuldu. Bir röportajcı, 'Her gün çalışacak mısın?' diye sordu. Ben de, 'Hayır hanımefendi—iş ve yaşam dengesi inançlıyım,' dedim. İki gün sonra, ortaklık teklifi alan bir telefon aldım. Temmuz 2020'de Austin, Texas bölgesi için resmi bir sözleşme imzaladık. Şirketim için ilk rotamı 22 Eylül 2020'de başlattım. Bugün, L2E Endüstrileri'ni—Learning 2 Exhale Industries'in kısaltması—sahibiyim ve Amazon benim ana taşıma müşterim. Üç yıldan az bir sürede 3 milyon doların üzerinde gelir elde ettik. Şimdi yanına 'Prime' yazılan 38 mavi kamyonet ve yaklaşık 80 çalışanım var. Ekibim, Amazon kargo istasyonlarından paketleri alır ve müşterilerin kapılarına veya iş yerlerine teslim eder—umuyorum ki gülümseyerek. Merkezi Texas bölgesinin bir kısmını hizmet veriyorum. Günlük 25-35 rota yönetiyorum ve kamyonetlerin hazır olduğunu ve çalışanların hazırlanmış olduğunu sağlıyorum. Arka planda, operasyonları yönetiyorum; kırsal, kentsel ve gelişmemiş bölgelere uygun rotalar planlıyorum. Amacımız, güvenliği ve kaliteyi maksimize ederek gelir elde etmek. Her teslimatta ödeme alıyoruz ve müşteri memnuniyetiyle ödüllendiriliyoruz. Her paket tesliminden sonra müşteriler, teslimatın zamanında olup olmadığı, sürücülerin ne kadar nazik davrandığı ve aşırı çaba gösterip göstermediği hakkında bir değerlendirme mesajı alıyorlar. Herkese cevap vermeyi teşvik ediyorum. Ödeme sistemi, müşteri memnuniyeti, teslimat kalitesi ve tutarlılıkla bağlantılı. Ancak iş büyümesini doğrudan kontrol etmiyorum—Amazon yapıyor. Bölgesel talebe ve paket hacmine göre ne kadar iş alacağımı belirliyorlar. 2024'te günlük 40 rota ortalama yapacağımızı söyleyemem. Ancak kazançlarımızın bir kısmını başka şirketler kurmak için yeniden yatıracağımı söyleyebilirim. Pozitif bir şirket kültürü oluşturmak, çalışanların zor zamanlarda kalmasına yardımcı olur—tam olarak bunu yaşadık. Şubat 2021'de, Texas'ta ölümcül bir kış fırtınası işletmeyi bir hafta boyunca durdurdu. Sonraki çeyrek felaket oldu. Emeklilik ve kişisel tasarruflarımı tahsis etmek zorunda kaldım ve çalışanlarımı ödemeye devam etmek için kendi maaşımı kesmem gerekiyordu. Sonunda Amazon'un sağladığı bir iş danışmanıyla 15 dakika görüşmek için oturdum. O, performans metriklerini analiz ederek işletmemi zorlayan düşük performanslı çalışanları belirledi. O andan itibaren, insanların duygularını önemsemek ile karlılık arasında denge kurmayı öğrendim. İyileştirme için açık süreler belirledim ve sürüş performansını değerlendirmek için standart puanlama sistemleri uyguladım. Ayrıca işletmenin sürdürülebilirliğini sağlamak için daha akıllı finansal kararlar almaya başladım. Bundan beri hiçbir maaş ödemesini ertelemedim ve kendi maaşımı yeniden almaya başladım. Başka bir yerde çalışanken, bazen kimse duygularımı önemsemezdi. Şimdi, kariyerim boyunca istediklerimi ekibime sunmaya çalışıyorum. Sadece kâr değil, bu işletmeye bağlı aileler yüzünden başarıya inançlıyım.

article_content: Twenty-five years ago, Marc Koska came across a chilling newspaper prediction: reused syringes would become a major driver of the AIDS epidemic. At the time, he found the idea unthinkable — but today, it’s a devastating reality. Each year, roughly 1.3 million people die from infections caused by unsafe injections, with a child losing their life every 24 seconds. The mechanism is horrifyingly simple: when a needle is reused, blood-borne pathogens like HIV and Hepatitis are passed directly from one person to another. Koska’s life changed in 1984 after reading that article while visiting home during a sailing trip in the Caribbean. Over the next 30 months, he immersed himself in research until he identified the solution: a syringe that could only be used once. He invented the K1 Auto-Disable syringe — a device that physically locks and breaks after a single injection, making reuse impossible. To scale this innovation, he founded Star Syringe, which now licenses the technology to 14 manufacturers supplying over 70 countries. Their efforts have helped save an estimated 9 million lives. Crucially, the syringe costs just 5 cents — less than a tenth of a Coke — yet delivers life-saving protection. Beyond manufacturing, Koska established SafePoint Trust in 2006 to drive policy reform and public awareness — not to sell syringes, but to ensure every injection is safe. In 2008, SafePoint launched a landmark campaign in India, reaching over half a billion people through press conferences, radio broadcasts, TV films, and cinema screenings, including the heartbreaking story of Sachin, a boy infected by a reused needle. The result? India’s government mandated AD syringes in all public clinics starting April 30, 2009. A second campaign in 2010 exposed lingering unsafe practices, and now, similar efforts are being adapted for Africa, targeting Swaziland, Tanzania, Nigeria, and Ghana. Hospitals report that for every dollar spent on these syringes, they save $280 in avoided treatment costs. Koska is now championing a universal ‘LifeSaver’ logo to make safe syringes instantly recognizable worldwide. He argues that unsafe injections are not mere negligence — they’re a form of mass harm, often stemming from lack of resources or education. His message is clear: change must come from the top down and the bottom up. And he’s ready to fight for it.
translated_content: Yirmi beş yıl önce, Marc Koska, yeniden kullanılan enjektörlerin AIDS salgınının ana nedeni olacağını öngören korkutucu bir gazete makalesiyle karşılaştı. O dönemde bu fikri düşünülemez buldu — ancak bugün bu korkunç bir gerçeklik. Her yıl yaklaşık 1,3 milyon kişi, güvenli olmayan enjeksiyonlardan kaynaklanan enfeksiyonlardan hayatını kaybediyor ve her 24 saniyede bir çocuk ölüyor. Mekanizma korkunç şekilde basit: İğne yeniden kullanıldığında, HIV ve Hepatit gibi kan yoluyla bulaşan patojenler doğrudan bir kişiden diğerine aktarılıyor. Koska'nın hayatı 1984'te Karayipler'de yelken açarken evine ziyarete gittiğinde o makaleyi okuduğunda değişti. Sonraki 30 ay boyunca araştırmaya daldı ve tek kullanımlık bir enjektörün çözüm olduğunu keşfetti. K1 Otomatik Devre Dışı Bırakan enjektörü icat etti — bu cihaz, tek bir enjeksiyondan sonra fiziksel olarak kilitlenir ve kırılır, böylece yeniden kullanım imkansız hale gelir. Bu yeniliği yaygınlaştırmak için Star Syringe'i kurdu ve şimdi bu teknolojiyi 70'ten fazla ülkeye tedarik eden 14 üreticiye lisans veriyor. Çabaları yaklaşık 9 milyon yaşamı kurtarmıştır. Önemli olan, enjektörün maliyetinin sadece 5 sent olması — bir Coca-Cola'nın onda birinden daha az — ama yine de hayati koruma sağlar. Üretimin ötesinde, Koska 2006'da her enjeksiyonun güvenli olmasını sağlamak için, enjektör satmak değil, politika reformu ve kamu bilincini artırmak amacıyla SafePoint Trust'u kurdu. 2008'de SafePoint, basın konferansları, radyo yayınları, TV ve sinema filmleri aracılığıyla Hindistan'da 500 milyondan fazla insana ulaşan efsanevi bir kampanya başlattı ve bu kampanyada, yeniden kullanılan bir iğneyle HIV bulaşan küçük Sachin'in acı verici hikayesi yer aldı. Sonuç? Hindistan hükümeti, 30 Nisan 2009'dan itibaren tüm kamu sağlık tesislerinde AD enjektörlerin kullanılmasını zorunlu kıldı. 2010'da yapılan ikinci bir kampanya, hâlâ devam eden güvenli olmayan uygulamaları ortaya çıkardı ve şimdi benzer çabalar, Afrika'da Swaziland, Tanzanya, Nijerya ve Gana'yı hedef alarak uyarlanıyor. Hastaneler, bu enjektörlere harcanan her doların, tedavi maliyetlerinden 280 dolar tasarruf sağladığını rapor ediyor. Koska, güvenli enjektörlerin hemen tanınabilir, istenebilir ve uygulanabilir hale gelmesi için evrensel bir 'LifeSaver' logosu öneriyor. Güvenli olmayan enjeksiyonların sadece ihmal olmadığını, genellikle kaynak eksikliği veya bilinçsizlikten kaynaklanan küresel bir zarar formu olduğunu savunuyor. Mesajı açık: Değişim hem üst düzeyden hem de alt düzeyden gelmeli. Ve mücadeleye hazır.

article_content: After a brief and turbulent nine-month marriage, former Welsh rugby star Andy Powell and his wife Natasha Gascoine have officially parted ways — with Gascoine taking her grievances public in a dramatic fashion. On social media, she shared intimate text exchanges that revealed Powell’s alleged infidelity and reckless behavior, calling him a liar, a cheat, and emotionally dishonest. In one message, he reportedly texted, 'I’m in Montpellier — just had a chance to bang a girl,' then immediately followed up with longing for her, a contradiction Gascoine found deeply hurtful. In response to what she describes as years of emotional manipulation and broken promises, Gascoine has listed nearly three dozen personal items related to their marriage on eBay — from her £10,000 Boodles engagement ring and £500 wedding dress to Powell’s worn rugby boots, match jerseys, and even his tailored wedding suit. Each listing includes a candid note, often laced with sarcasm, such as describing his suit as 'designed by the very talented Tony Q'aja & team' — a jab at his inflated ego. She explicitly states that these objects no longer hold sentimental value and that proceeds will support Women’s Aid and the Samaritans. Gascoine, a 25-year-old office worker from Monmouthshire, said she felt compelled to speak out after realizing Powell had constructed a false image to win admiration. 'He’s built a character to fool everyone who knows him. I fell for it,' she wrote. She also referenced his long-standing issues: a 2010 conviction for stealing a shopping cart to buy snacks at 5 a.m., a 2011 bar fight suspension, and his erratic conduct during his brief stint with Wigan Warriors, where he played just five games before being released. Though Powell, 32, once earned 23 caps for Wales and toured with the British and Irish Lions in 2009, his legacy is increasingly overshadowed by his off-field troubles. Friends say he’s attempting a return to rugby union, but Gascoine insists his public persona is designed to feed his need for validation. 'I know he’d love his name being mentioned,' she wrote. 'He loves the ego boost.' Her final act? Selling the symbols of their failed union — not for profit, but as a symbolic severance.

article_content: Experts believe the 298 passengers and crew aboard Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 were likely unaware of the catastrophe as the aircraft was struck by an SA-11 Buk missile — also known as a Grizzly or Gadfly — which instantly shredded the plane. Designed to destroy aircraft, the missile detonated approximately 20 meters from the Boeing 777, releasing a ring of high-velocity shrapnel that pierced the fuselage, wings, engines, and fuel tanks. The resulting explosion caused immediate decompression and fire, rendering those on board unconscious within milliseconds. The SA-11, developed by the Soviet Union in 1979, is a mobile surface-to-air system capable of reaching altitudes up to 75,000 feet. It takes about five minutes to prepare for launch and can strike targets at speeds exceeding Mach 3, hitting MH17 just eight seconds after firing. According to Justin Bronk of the Royal United Services Institute, the widespread debris field confirms the missile’s destructive pattern. The aircraft’s pressurized cabin would have ruptured violently, leading to catastrophic structural failure. The missile was reportedly launched from a separatist-controlled area near Torez in eastern Ukraine. Western governments, including the UK, have stated it is 'increasingly likely' that pro-Russian militants fired the weapon. Rescue teams, including coal miners and emergency workers, combed through sunflower fields and villages for victims and belongings. Personal items — from children’s books to vinyl records — were found scattered across the site, many untouched by flames. Eyewitnesses described bodies falling from the sky 'like rags.' One resident reported a corpse crashing through her kitchen roof. Makeshift white flags marked burial spots, and some bodies were covered with plastic sheeting weighted by stones, one adorned with a single flower. The flight had been cleared by the International Civil Aviation Organization, and no distress call was received before the crash. The Buk system’s identification protocols could not distinguish civilian aircraft from military targets, raising concerns about operational safety in conflict zones.
translated_content: Uzmanlar, 298 yolcunun ve mürettebatın, bir SA-11 Buk füzesi — aynı zamanda Grizzly ya da Gadfly olarak bilinen — tarafından uçağın anında parçalanması sırasında felaketin farkında olmadığını düşünüyor. Uçağı yok etmek için tasarlanan füze, Boeing 777'den yaklaşık 20 metre uzaklıkta patladı ve gövde, kanatlar, motorlar ve yakıt tanklarını delen yüksek hızda bir parçacık halkası saldı. Sonuçta oluşan patlama, anında hava basıncının düşmesine ve yangına neden oldu ve yolcuları milisaniyeler içinde bilinçsiz hale getirdi. 1979 yılında Sovyetler Birliği tarafından geliştirilen SA-11, 75.000 fit yüksekliğe ulaşabilen hareketli bir yüzeyden havaya fırlatılan sistemdir. Hazırlık süreci yaklaşık beş dakika sürer ve Mach 3'ün üzerindeki hızlarda hedeflere vurabilir; MH17'e fırlatıldıktan sadece sekiz saniye sonra ulaştı. Royal United Services Institute'tan Justin Bronk, geniş yayılımlı çöp alanının füzenin yıkıcı desenini doğruladığını söylüyor. Uçağın basınçlı kabininin şiddetle çatlaması ve kritik yapısal hasar oluştuğunu belirtiyor. Füzenin doğu Ukrayna'daki Torez yakınlarında bir ayrılıkçı kontrol bölgesinde ateşlendiği bildirildi. İngiltere de dahil batılı hükümetler, bu silahın pro-Rusya militanlar tarafından ateşlendiğinin 'giderek daha olası' olduğunu ifade ediyor. Kömür madencileri ve acil durum ekipleri, kurbanları ve eşyaları aramak için ayçiçek tarlaları ve köyleri taradı. Çocuk kitaplarından vinil plaklara kadar kişisel eşyalar, sahada dağılmış halde bulundu, çoğu yangından korunmuştu. Gözlemciler, bedenlerin 'bez gibi' gökyüzünden düştüğünü anlattı. Bir yerli, bir cesedin mutfak çatısından geçip içine düştüğünü söyledi. Geçici beyaz bayraklar mezar yerlerini işaretledi ve bazı cesetler taşlarla ağırlanan plastik örtülerle kaplandı, biri bir çiçekle anıldı. Uçuş, Uluslararası Sivil Havacılık Örgütü tarafından güvenli ilan edilmiş ve felaketten önce hiçbir acil çağrı alınmamıştı. Buk sisteminin tanıma protokolleri sivil uçakları askeri hedeflerden ayıramazdı, bu da çatışma bölgelerinde operasyonel güvenlik konusunda endişeler uyandırıyor.

article_content: A high-stakes digital manhunt is unfolding online as cybersecurity experts race to stop Conficker C — a sophisticated worm programmed to activate on April 1, 2009 — before it can compromise millions of computers worldwide. Researchers at CA discovered that the worm’s code includes a trigger set for April Fool’s Day, prompting a coordinated response from global security teams who’ve formed the Conficker Cabal. Their mission: track down the author, neutralize the threat, and minimize damage. Motivated by a $250,000 bounty from Microsoft and a shared sense of digital justice, members of the Cabal — many of whom are former hackers themselves — view dismantling the worm as a badge of honor. 'We love catching bad guys,' said Alvin Estevez, CEO of Enigma Software Group. 'We slap each other five when we kill an infection.' Already believed to have infected between 5 and 10 million machines, Conficker C remains stealthy — no obvious symptoms yet. But on April 1, it may unleash a range of destructive actions: deleting files, hijacking infected 'zombie' PCs to crash websites, stealing passwords, or tricking users into buying fake antivirus software. Experts agree that modern malware is less about chaos and more about profit. Conficker C hides deeply within systems, blocks Windows updates, and constantly evolves to outsmart countermeasures. 'It’s a cat-and-mouse game,' said Don DeBolt of CA. The worm’s author remains anonymous, but investigators suspect ties to Eastern European regions where law enforcement oversight is weak. Researchers are comparing Conficker C’s code to past malware, searching for coding fingerprints — though catching the culprit is considered unlikely unless they make a mistake. The latest version, Conficker C, generates 50,000 unique domain names daily — a massive leap from the 250 used by its predecessor — rendering previous takedown strategies ineffective. Microsoft urges users to check for recent Windows updates: if none arrived in March, their system may be compromised. Those concerned should visit http://safety.live.com. While the first strain of Conficker exploited a vulnerability in a cryptographic function developed by MIT’s Dr. Ronald Rivest, experts emphasize that open-source technologies enable far more good than harm. 'Any technology can be used for good or evil,' Rivest said. 'This is just an example.' Despite the odds, the Conficker Cabal remains determined. 'The best minds in the industry are working on this to protect customers,' DeBolt said. 'We’re trying to reduce the impact — but we know this malware will keep evolving.'

article_content: Kevin Davies, a rugged striker who spent over a decade in the Premier League, doesn’t mince words: defenders have been getting away with too much inside the penalty area for far too long. Whether it’s at corners or free-kicks, he recalls being held, elbowed, stamped on, and scratched — sometimes by three men at once — all while trying to get a shot off. He estimates he missed out on at least 50 penalties because officials were afraid to call them. Now 37 and still playing for Preston North End, Davies is caught between two truths. He admires the raw, physical style that defines English football — and he’d happily have a defender like the ones who tormented him on his own team. But he also knows that honest forwards like him are being systematically blocked out, not just challenged. 'They’re not even looking for the ball,' he says. 'Their only job is to stop you from getting space.' Davies never pretended to be hurt to win a penalty. He was too proud to dive. Even when he was being manhandled, he stood his ground — which made the lack of whistle even more galling. 'If it’s a foul on the halfway line, why isn’t it a foul in the box?' he asks. His former boss at Bolton, Sam Allardyce, even compiled a dossier of Davies’ injuries — including photos of neck scratches — and sent it to referees’ officials. Still, nothing changed. And while some defenders like Gary Cahill and managers such as Manuel Pellegrini are now backing Sportsmail’s 'Hands Off In The Box' campaign, Davies worries that referees might overcorrect, punishing innocent challenges just to appear fair. He remembers being sent off after barely touching Amdy Faye — while Hermann Hreidarsson got red-carded for a brutal elbow that broke Davies’ cheekbone. 'It’s not about making things even,' he warns. 'It’s about calling what’s actually happening.' Davies hopes stricter enforcement will curb the worst excesses — not eliminate physicality, but restore fairness. After all, he says, if defenders are taught to ‘stop anyone, any way,’ then the rules need to catch up.

article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) — A new study suggests that parents who use forward-facing strollers may unintentionally hinder their child’s emotional and social development. According to research published Friday by Dundee University’s School of Psychology, babies who face away from their caregivers interact far less with them — speaking, laughing, and responding less frequently. The study, which surveyed 2,722 parent-child pairs, found that simply turning the stroller to face the parent doubled the amount of verbal interaction. In a controlled experiment involving 20 infants, researchers observed that when babies faced their parents during a one-mile walk, they exhibited fewer signs of stress and more vocal engagement. Dr. Suzanne Zeedyk, the lead developmental psychologist, stated, 'For many babies today, life in a forward-facing buggy is emotionally impoverished and possibly stressful.' She added, 'Stressed babies grow into anxious adults.' The findings reveal that 62% of all children in the study rode in forward-facing strollers — rising to 86% among toddlers aged one to two. UK child education advocates at the Sutton Trust have urged manufacturers to reconsider stroller design to prioritize face-to-face interaction.

article_content: People often speak of a bird’s-eye view—but one animal lover in Montreal wanted to experience the world from a squirrel’s perspective. David Freiheit attached a slice of bread to a GoPro camera, hoping an inquisitive squirrel might pick it up and carry it away while recording. What happened next exceeded his expectations. A curious squirrel approached from a nearby tree, sniffed the device cautiously, and after determining it posed no threat, seized the camera and sprinted up a tree. The resulting footage offered a bumpy, thrilling ride through the canopy—unintentionally capturing Freiheit waiting patiently below, hoping for the camera’s return. After examining the unfamiliar object, the squirrel ultimately decided it wasn’t edible and dropped it to the ground. Luckily, the GoPro survived the fall. A quick blow on the lens cleared away the dust, and the camera was ready to use again.

Jane Ellison, MP and former health minister, revealed at a Tory Reform Group meeting that while policy preparations were complete, she was instructed to wait before speaking publicly. When asked if this meant No. 10 was blocking the move, she replied, 'I couldn't possibly comment,' drawing laughter from attendees. This admission follows an open letter signed by over 600 clinicians published in the British Medical Journal, which states: 'Smoking-related disease remains the main cause of preventable deaths in the UK, killing more than 100,000 people annually. Ending the marketing of tobacco through branded packaging is both necessary and logical.' Ellison herself believes plain packaging would likely improve public health. However, some Conservative colleagues argue it could harm small retailers like newsagents. Meanwhile, Labour has pointed to political strategist Lynton Crosby — who has previously worked for tobacco companies — as a possible influence behind the delay. Labour’s Shadow Minister for Public Health, Luciana Berger, condemned the delay: 'We now know the hold-up comes from Downing Street. There can be no excuse for further delay. This is what Parliament voted for, what health professionals demand, and what the public supports. Cameron must stand up for public health, not vested interests.' A No. 10 spokesperson denied allegations of obstruction, stating: 'It is not true that any attempt is being made to block this measure.' Jane Ellison was unavailable for further comment.

article_content: Ever heard of companies convinced they’ve invented the next big thing—only to realize no one actually wants it? Many businesses fall into a linear mindset, assuming they know best, and miss the transformative power of engaging real users and stakeholders. This isn’t just a missed opportunity—it’s a recipe for failure. Co-creation, by contrast, unlocks innovation that’s truly aligned with human needs. Shelly Tsui, a final-year doctoral researcher at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), has spent years studying this very concept. Today, she defended her thesis. 'I’m very excited,' she says. 'It’s time to wrap up five and a half years of work and share it with everyone.' What does co-creation mean? The definition varies by field—designers, strategists, engineers all see it differently—but at its core, it’s when diverse groups come together to build something valuable, collectively. Yes, more companies are catching on. Brands like Lego, Starbucks, and IKEA thrive by letting customers co-design products. Take IKEA: People don’t just buy furniture—they assemble it. That hands-on experience creates emotional connection and perceived value. In Eindhoven, citizens partnered with local government and designers to co-create smart street lighting for their neighborhoods—'Lighting Up the City.' The result? Better lighting, stronger community ties, and improved quality of life. In healthcare, the stakes are higher. Startups developing medical devices must involve patients from day one. Every patient is unique. Skipping their input doesn’t just mean poor design—it risks real harm. But co-creation isn’t easy. It’s messy, slow, and hard to manage. That’s why so many organizations stick to simple, linear innovation models—four neat stages, clear milestones. Unfortunately, those models ignore the messy reality of human collaboration. Shelly’s message to companies? Stop treating co-creation like a checkbox. Don’t just ask users for feedback at the end. Involve them from the start. Are citizens helping shape the vision of a city redevelopment? Or were they invited only after the plan was already set? She dreams of a future where end-users don’t just respond—they lead. Where they sit at the table with executives and designers, shaping strategy alongside them. After her PhD, Shelly plans to leave academia and bring her insights to management consultancies or creative agencies. There, she hopes to help clients—from governments to nonprofits—co-create solutions not just for profit, but for society: tackling climate change, inequality, and sustainability through true collaboration.

Eindhoven Üniversitesi Teknoloji (TU/e)'de son sınıf doktora araştırmacısı olan Shelly Tsui, bu kavramı yıllardır inceledi. Bugün tezini savundu. 'Çok heyecanlıyım,' diyor. 'Beş buçuk yıllık çalışmayı bitirip herkese paylaşmak zamanı.' Ortak yaratım nedir? Tanım alanlara göre değişir—tasarımcılar, stratejistler, mühendisler farklı şekilde görürler—ancak temelinde, çeşitli grupların birlikte değerli bir şey oluşturmasıdır. Evet, daha fazla şirket bunu anlamaya başlıyor. Lego, Starbucks ve IKEA gibi markalar, müşterilerin ürünleri birlikte tasarlamasına izin vererek başarı elde ediyor. Eindhoven'de vatandaşlar, yerel hükümet ve tasarımcılarla birlikte mahallelerinde akıllı sokak aydınlatması oluşturmak için iş birliği yaptılar—'Şehri Aydınlatma.' Sonuç? Daha iyi aydınlatma, daha güçlü topluluk bağları ve yaşam kalitesinde iyileşme. Sağlık sektöründe riskler daha yüksektir. Tıbbi cihazlar geliştiren girişimciler, hastaları ilk günden itibaren dahil etmelidir. Her hasta benzersizdir. Onların girdisini atlamak sadece kötü tasarım demek değildir—gerçek zararlara yol açabilir. Ancak ortak yaratım kolay değildir. Karışık, yavaş ve yönetimi zordur. Bu yüzden birçok kuruluş basit, doğrusal yenilik modellerine—dört net aşama, net aşamalar—tutunur. Ne yazık ki bu modeller insan iş birliğinin karmaşık gerçekliğini görmezden gelir. Shelly'nin şirketlere mesajı? Ortak yaratımı bir kontrol listesi gibi değil. Sadece son aşamada geri bildirim istemeyin. Onları baştan dahil edin. Vatandaşlar, bir şehir yenileme projesinin vizyonunu şekillendirmekte mi? Yoksa plan zaten hazırlandıktan sonra mı davet edildiler? O, son kullanıcıların sadece yanıt vermekten öteye geçip liderlik ettiği bir gelecek hayal ediyor. Onlar, yönetici ve tasarımcılarla birlikte stratejiyi şekillendirmek için masada oturuyor. Doktorasını tamamladıktan sonra, Shelly akademiden ayrılmayı ve bilgilerini yönetim danışmanlığı firmalarına veya yaratıcı ajanslara taşımayı planlıyor. Orada, hükümetlerden kamu kurumlarına kadar müşterilerine, iklim değişikliği, eşitsizlik ve sürdürülebilirlik gibi toplumsal sorunları çözmek için gerçek iş birliği yoluyla çözümler yaratmaya yardımcı olmayı umuyor.

article_content: Fantasy writer Terry Pratchett, best known for his beloved Discworld series, has revealed he was diagnosed with a rare type of early-onset Alzheimer’s. Despite the diagnosis, the 59-year-old author insists he has no plans to stop writing—his iconic books have sold over 45 million copies across 33 languages, and he’s already laying the groundwork for his next two projects: 'Nation' and 'Unseen Academicals'. In a candid post on illustrator Paul Kidby’s website, titled 'an embuggerance,' Pratchett explained that while he’d preferred to keep the news private, obligations to fans, publishers, and convention organizers made transparency necessary. 'All other things being equal,' he wrote, 'I expect to meet most of my commitments.' He asked his audience to stay upbeat: 'I think there’s time for at least a few more books yet.' In a poignant yet wry footnote, he added, 'This should be interpreted as 'I am not dead.' Of course, I will die—like everyone else—but not today.' Pratchett, who started his career as a newspaper reporter in the 1960s and was knighted with the Order of the British Empire in 1998 for his literary contributions, described the Discworld books as having begun as a spoof of 1980s fantasy tropes—and morphed into something far stranger and deeper. 'Even I don’t know what it is now,' he mused. He closed with a humorous plea: 'If you’re wondering what you can do, skip the sympathy cards—get me a top neuroscientist instead.'

article_content: JERUSALEM (CNN) — The Israeli navy intercepted a vessel attempting to breach its maritime blockade of Gaza on Tuesday, seizing control of the boat and detaining its crew, according to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF). The Free Gaza Movement, a human rights group that organized the mission, identified the vessel as the 'Spirit of Humanity' and claimed it was carrying humanitarian aid, along with former U.S. Congresswoman Cynthia McKinney and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Mairead Maguire. The IDF stated that it had contacted the vessel — which it referred to as the 'Arion' — while it was still at sea and issued repeated warnings that entry into Gazan waters was prohibited due to security risks and the ongoing naval blockade. Despite these warnings, the boat proceeded into restricted waters, prompting the IDF to intercept, board, and redirect it to the port of Ashdod. McKinney, who served six terms representing Georgia and was the Green Party’s 2008 presidential nominee, and Maguire, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1976 for her peace activism in Northern Ireland, were among the 20 people taken into custody, according to the Free Gaza Movement. In a statement relayed by the group, McKinney condemned the action as 'an outrageous violation of international law,' asserting that the vessel was never in Israeli waters and was on a peaceful human rights mission. She urged the international community to demand their release so the mission could continue. McKinney’s father, former Georgia state legislator Billy McKinney, said he received a brief call from his daughter around 3 a.m. Tuesday, during which she assured him she was 'OK' before the line went dead as Israeli forces boarded the ship. He added that while the U.S. State Department provided contact information for the U.S. Embassy in Israel, no response had been received by Tuesday night. The IDF confirmed the incident and stated that all humanitarian aid destined for Gaza must be delivered through authorized land crossings with prior coordination. The aid aboard the intercepted vessel, they said, would be delivered to Gaza 'subject to authorization.' The Free Gaza Movement noted this was the eighth such voyage it has attempted since its founding; five have succeeded, while previous efforts in January and December 2008 were blocked by Israeli forces.

article_content: A dream 50th birthday trip to New York for 15 lifelong school friends turned into a nightmare after they lost £11,000 when their travel agent went bust. Organiser Mandy Weston, 50, saved for three years to take her friends on a joint birthday celebration in New York. But she was left seething when Kent-based Blue Skies Travel (UK) Ltd went into liquidation — leaving their Big Apple trip in jeopardy. The 15 friends eventually made it to New York — but only after a friend loaned them the money to rebook at double the original cost. Each friend had paid £750 for the three-day trip. They paid their deposit via protected Visa cards, but the bulk of the payment was made by bank transfer after the company promised £70 in travel vouchers for early payment. Mandy Weston had paid for flights, hotels, and theatre tickets — but the company had booked nothing and paid not a single penny to any vendor. Blue Skies Travel (UK) Ltd, registered with ATOL, collapsed just weeks before departure. The company now owes consumers nearly £415,000 in unbooked holidays. Mandy said: 'I am seething. What breaks my heart is how they can get away with ripping off £415,000 from people. This was a holiday of a lifetime — but some people lost their weddings. I can't believe no one raised suspicions. I don't think there's a hope in hell of us getting our money back.' Although they had a great time in New York, Mandy added: 'It has cost us a lot — in money, worry, and pain.' The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA), which oversees ATOL, confirmed it has received multiple complaints about Blue Skies Travel and is investigating. Scotland Yard is also investigating allegations of fraud against the Kent-based company. No arrests have been made yet. It should be noted that this company is not affiliated with Blue Skies Travel in Cardiff. However, it shares phone numbers and operational links with other suspect firms: Bright Skies Travel and Fly Vacations. Online reviews on TripAdvisor are overflowing with similar stories. Users report fake booking confirmations, ignored calls, and unpaid reservations — even after providing payment proof. One reviewer, Thomas D from Belfast, said: 'United Airlines confirmed Clive never paid for our flights. He’s now ignoring all messages.' Bernadette C from Blackpool added: 'Jet2.com has no record of our booking. I’m filing a fraud report with the police.' The company’s Kent office is believed closed, its website offline. Despite repeated attempts, MailOnline could not reach Clive Allard. If you’ve been affected by Blue Skies Travel (UK) Ltd, contact John Hutchinson at john.hutchinson@dailymail.co.uk.

article_content: The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge celebrated the news of her pregnancy with a home-cooked shepherd’s pie and an early night, according to a close friend. Former school friend Jessica Hay said the couple discovered Kate’s pregnancy in October at their three-bedroom cottage in Wales, calling it 'the most nerve-racking moment of Kate’s entire life.' Contrary to expectations, there were no champagne corks popped—instead, the pair enjoyed a quiet meal and retired early. In an exclusive interview with Australian magazine New Idea, Hay also recounted how Kate fell seriously ill in early December, prompting a visit to the private King Edward VII Hospital. Kate was diagnosed with hyperemesis gravidarum, a severe form of morning sickness. After treatment, she began recovering and is now craving foods like papaya. The couple had planned to announce the pregnancy on Christmas Eve but shared the news sooner after Kate’s hospitalization, as they found keeping the secret emotionally taxing. They visited Kate’s parents, Carole and Michael Middleton, at their home in Bucklebury, Berkshire, shortly before her illness. Though speculation has arisen that the pregnancy may involve twins—a possibility her circle finds plausible—Prince William and Kate have asked doctors not to disclose the baby’s sex and have not purchased any baby clothing. They intend to wait until birth to learn the gender, staying true to tradition. Hay suggests potential names include Diana and Victoria, noting that Kate has long admired the name Diana. Kate plans to be a hands-on mother, preferring a home filled with laughter over one staffed with nannies, governesses, or butlers. According to Hay, the couple used a standard over-the-counter pregnancy test to confirm the news, which revealed the thin blue line they had hoped for.

article_content: On Tuesday night at Pratt Institute, filmmaker Spike Lee delivered a passionate critique of gentrification in New York City, responding to a question about recent media portrayals that frame urban renewal positively. Speaking with raw emotion, Lee confronted an audience member who defended the transformation of neighborhoods like Harlem and Fort Greene. 'Let me just kill you right now,' he snapped, referencing the stark contrast between today’s manicured public spaces and the neglected streets of his youth. He painted a vivid picture of Fort Greene Park in the early morning—now filled with dogs and pristine walkways—as a surreal spectacle, comparing it to the Westminster Dog Show. 'That’s not the Brooklyn I knew,' he said. Back then, garbage piled up for days, schools were underfunded, and police presence was nearly nonexistent. Now, he noted, the arrival of affluent white residents seems to trigger immediate upgrades—clean streets, better services, louder enforcement—while the original communities are pushed aside. Lee emphasized that these changes aren’t just physical—they’re cultural. He recalled decades-long drum circles in Mount Morris Park being shut down because neighbors complained about noise. He mentioned a planned tribute to Michael Jackson in Fort Greene Park that was canceled due to fears of litter. 'We didn’t have this problem before,' he said. 'Now, if you’re not quiet, you’re the problem.' He invoked his 1989 film 'Do the Right Thing,' pointing to a scene where a white man scuffs his new sneakers on a Black neighbor’s sidewalk—an act that sparks tension—as eerily prophetic. 'That scene was a crystal ball,' he claimed. 'It showed us what was coming.' Lee also shared a personal story: his father, a jazz musician, bought a home in 1968. Decades later, new neighbors called the police—not because he was causing trouble, but because he played acoustic bass. 'He doesn’t even use electricity!' Lee exclaimed. 'And now you call the cops in 2013? Get outta here.' He condemned the attitude of newcomers who act like pioneers discovering unclaimed land. 'You didn’t find this,' he said. 'People lived here for generations. You don’t get to erase our culture and call it progress.' Yet, despite his fiery rhetoric, Lee himself moved to the Upper East Side in 2000. Still, his production company remains rooted in Fort Greene—a symbolic anchor to the community he defends. 'I believe in democracy,' he concluded. 'Everyone deserves a place to live. But you’ve got to show respect. You can’t just move in and decide everything has to change because you’re here.'
translated_content: Salı gecesi Pratt Enstitüsü'nde sinema yapımcısı Spike Lee, kent yenileme olgusunu olumlu sunan son medya haberlerine yanıt olarak New York City'deki gentrifikasyona karşı tutkulu bir eleştiri sundu. Sert bir dille, Harlem ve Fort Greene gibi mahallelerin dönüşümünü savunan bir izleyiciye cevap verdi. 'Şimdi seni öldürsem ne olur,' dedi, bugünün düzenli halk mekanları ile gençlik yıllarında gördüğü terk edilmiş sokaklar arasındaki keskin farka işaret ederek. Fort Greene Park'ın sabah saatlerindeki durumunu—şimdi köpeklerle dolu, mükemmel yürüyüş yollarıyla—bir Westminster Köpek Gösterisi gibi tuhaf bir spektakül olarak betimledi. 'Bu benim bildiğim Brooklyn değil,' dedi. O zamanlar çöpler günlerce birikirdi, okullar yetersizdi ve polis varlığı neredeyse yoktu. Şimdi ise, zengin beyaz yeni yerleşenlerin gelmesi, temiz sokaklar, daha iyi hizmetler, daha güçlü uygulama gibi anında iyileştirmeleri tetikliyor—ama orijinal topluluklar kenara itiliyor. Lee, bu değişimlerin sadece fiziksel olmadığını, kültürel olduğunu da vurguladı. Mount Morris Park'ta onlarca yıldır devam eden Afrikalı davulların sesiyle ilgili şikayetler nedeniyle kapatıldığını anlattı. Michael Jackson'in ölümüne saygıda bulunmak için Fort Greene Park'ta düzenlenmek istenen bir etkinliğin çöp korkusu nedeniyle iptal edildiğini de belirtti. 'Bundan önce böyle bir sorunumuz yoktu,' dedi. 'Şimdi sessiz değilsen, sen sorunsun.' 1989'da çıkan 'Do the Right Thing' filmini çağrıştırdı; beyaz bir adamın siyah komşusunun yeni Air Jordan ayakkabılarına leke bırakmasıyla başlayan gerilimi, geleceğin öngörüsü olarak gösterdi. 'Bu sahne bir kristal topdu,' dedi. 'Ne olacağını göstermişti.' Lee ayrıca babasının, bir caz müzisyeni olan, 1968 yılında bir ev satın aldığını anlattı. Onlarca yıl sonra, yeni komşular onun akustik bas çaldığı için polisi çağırdı. 'O elektrikli bas bile çalmıyor!' diye bağırdı Lee. 'Ve şimdi 2013'te polisi mi çağırıyorsunuz? Buradan çıkın!' Yeni yerleşenlerin, boş arazi keşfediyor gibi davranmasını kınadı. 'Sen bunu bulmadın,' dedi. 'Burada nesillerdir insanlar yaşıyordu. Kültürümüzü silip ilerleme diye adlandıramazsın.' Ancak, sert söylemlerine rağmen, Lee kendi başına 2000'den beri Upper East Side'da yaşıyor. Yine de, ürettiği şirketin merkezi Fort Greene'de kalıyor—savunduğu topluluğa sembolik bir bağ. 'Demokrasiye inanıyorum,' diye sonuçlandırdı. 'Herkesin yaşaması için bir yer olması lazım. Ama saygı göstermen gerek. Sen gelip her şeyin değişmesini gerektirirsin çünkü buradasın mı? Hayır, yapamazsın.'

article_content: Michael Bay, the director behind explosive blockbusters like Transformers, found himself unexpectedly out of his element—not on a battlefield of robots or sinking ships, but on a stage at CES. During a live unveiling of Samsung’s new 105-inch curved UHD TV, Bay paused when his teleprompter glitched. What began as a heartfelt monologue about storytelling and cinematic escape quickly unraveled as the text on screen flickered and jumped. Flustered, he turned to Samsung executive Joe Stinziano and said, 'The type is all off—I’ll just wing this.' Moments later, he stepped away from the podium, apologizing to the audience. In a candid blog post afterward, Bay admitted he’d been so eager to speak that he skipped the intro, and when the teleprompter malfunctioned, he chose to leave. 'I guess live shows aren’t my thing,' he wrote. Online reactions were divided: some joked, with accounts like Funny or Die quipping, 'No script, big explosion, disappointed audience—dude’s still got it!' Others, including filmmaker Zak Bagans, offered support, reminding people that even the most creative minds can battle anxiety. Notably, Samsung made no mention of Bay in its official press release about the TV.

Samsung'un yeni 105 inç eğri UHD televizyonunun canlı tanıtımında, teleprompter arızalandığında Bay duraksadı. Sinemada hikâye anlatma ve izleyicinin dünyadan kaçmasına yardımcı olma üzerine başladığı samimi bir monolog, ekrandaki metinlerin titremesi ve sıçramasıyla hızla bozuldu. Şaşkın bir şekilde, Samsung üst düzey yöneticisi Joe Stinziano'ya dönerek, 'Metinler tamamen karışık—ben bunu serbestçe yapacağım,' dedi. Birkaç saniye sonra sahneyi terk etti ve izleyicilere özür diledi. 'Sanırım canlı gösteriler benim için değil,' yazdı. Çevrimiçi tepkiler bölündü: bazıları, Funny or Die hesabının 'Hiç senaryo yok, büyük patlama, hayal kırıklığına uğrayan bir izleyici kitlesi—adam hala işini yapıyor!' diye alaycı bir yorum yapmasıyla gülüyordu. Diğerleri, özellikle sinema yapımcısı Zak Bagans, en yaratıcı zihinlerin bile kaygıyla mücadele edebileceğini hatırlatarak destek verdi. Dikkat çekici bir şekilde, Samsung resmi basın açıklamasında Bay'den hiçbir şekilde bahsetmedi.

article_content: An 86-year-old World War II veteran, Paul Browning, is recovering after being violently attacked outside Good Samaritan Hospital in Cincinnati, Ohio. Authorities say the assault occurred Sunday as Browning was heading to his car after visiting his wife of 65 years, Ilda Browning, who is recovering from surgery. Thirty-year-old Craig Phelps was arrested and charged with robbery and possession of drug paraphernalia, including a needle used for heroin. According to a police affidavit, Phelps slammed Browning against a wall, causing severe facial injuries that required stitches and left him badly bruised and swollen. In a remarkable display of compassion, Browning reportedly helped Phelps to his feet after the attack and apologized, telling him he thought he was someone else. Browning’s son, Marvin, shared the account with local station WLWT, describing his father as unshakably resilient. Though initially treated for his injuries, doctors later discovered Browning has an irregular heartbeat and will require heart surgery. Despite this, family members say he remains optimistic, repeating, 'Everything’s OK.' Phelps, a father and construction foreman, was apprehended in the hospital parking lot. Officers brought him to Browning’s hospital room for identification while the veteran received care. Phelps is being held on a $25,000 bond and is scheduled to return to court on September 10. Publicly available photos from Phelps’ Facebook page show him posing with multiple firearms and tactical equipment, adding further context to the case.

Yetkililer, saldırganın Pazar günü Browning’in arabasına doğru yürüdüğünü fark ettiğini belirtti. 30 yaşındaki Craig Phelps, soygun ve eroin kullanımı için kullanılan bir iğneyle ilgili uyuşturucu aleti bulundurma suçlarıyla tutuklandı. Polis raporuna göre, Phelps, Browning’i duvara çarparak ciddi yüz yaraları yarattı. Yaralar dikiş gerektirdi ve Browning ciddi morluklar ve şişlikler yaşadı. İlginç bir şekilde, Browning saldırıdan sonra Phelps’e yardım ederek onu kaldırdı ve 'Seni başkasıyla karıştırdım' dedi. Oğlu Marvin, WLWT’ye babasının olaydan sonra bile nezaketini koruduğunu anlattı. Yaralarının tedavisi sırasında doktorlar, Browning’in düzensiz kalp atışları olduğunu tespit etti ve kalp ameliyatına ihtiyacı olacağını bildirdi. Ailesi, Browning’in 'Her şey yolunda' diyerek umutlu kaldığını ve iyileşeceği konusunda emin olduklarını ifade etti. Phelps, bir baba ve inşaat şefi olarak, hastane otoparkında tutuklandı. Polisler, Browning tedavi alırken onu hastane odasına getirip tanıtmayı başardı. Phelps, 25.000 dolarlık kefaletle tutuklu durumda ve 10 Eylül’de mahkemeye tekrar çıkacak. Phelps’in Facebook sayfasından erişilebilir fotoğraflar, onun çatışma tüfekleri, tabancalar ve taktik ekipmanlarla poz verdiğini gösteriyor.

article_content: A second woman in Southern California has accused a former teacher of sexual abuse, adding to growing allegations that led to the educator’s resignation last week. The teacher stepped down from her position at Alhambra Unified School District after a 28-year-old woman posted a YouTube video in which she described being abused starting at age 12 — and in which the teacher can be heard admitting to the misconduct. The new accuser, now 18, filed a formal complaint this week against Val Verde Unified School District, alleging negligence during the 2009–2010 school year when she was a 14-year-old middle school student. Speaking at a press conference alongside her attorney, she described years of emotional manipulation: the teacher convinced her that her family didn’t care, that she was alone, and that the educator was her only source of love and support. She said the abuse was not always physical, but threats — including claims the teacher would kill herself if she left — kept her silent for years. 'This should have never happened,' she told reporters. 'If the district had done its job, none of this would have occurred.' Her legal team is also pursuing a claim against Riverside Unified School District, which previously employed the teacher and allegedly provided positive references despite prior concerns. Riverside officials confirmed receipt of the claim but declined to comment. Riverside Police launched an investigation following the YouTube video in January and have since confirmed a second victim has come forward. Detectives are now examining both cases. While the statute of limitations may limit criminal charges, investigators say they are exploring all possible offenses based on evidence. The teacher has not responded to repeated requests for comment from CNN. Advocates for the victims hope the case sparks legislative reform to better protect students and hold institutions accountable.

Öğretmen, 28 yaşındaki bir kadın tarafından 12 yaşında olduğunda taciz edildiğini anlatan bir YouTube videosu yayınladıktan sonra Alhambra Birleşik Okul Bölgesi'ndeki görevinden istifa etti — ve bu videoda öğretmenin tacizi kabul ettiği duyulabiliyor. Yeni iddia eden kadın, şimdi 18 yaşında, 2009-2010 eğitim yılında 14 yaşındaki bir ortaokul öğrencisiyken taciz yaşadığı iddiasıyla Val Verde Birleşik Okul Bölgesi'ne karşı resmi bir şikâyette bulundu. Avukatıyla bir basın toplantısında konuşan kadın, yıllarca duygusal manipülasyon yaşadığını anlattı: öğretmen, ailesinin ilgilenmediğini, yalnız olduğunu ve kendisinin tek sevgi ve destek kaynağı olduğunu söyleyerek onu ikna etmişti. Kadın, tacizin her zaman fiziksel olmadığını, ancak öğretmenin 'eğer gidersen kendini öldüreceğim' gibi tehditlerle sessiz kalmasını sağladığını söyledi. 'Bu asla olmamalıydı,' dedi gazetecilere. 'Eğer okul yönetimi görevini yapmış olsaydı, bunların hiçbiri olmazdı.' Avukat ekibi aynı zamanda, öğretmenin daha önce çalıştığı ve önceden endişeler olmasına rağmen pozitif referanslar verdiği Riverside Birleşik Okul Bölgesi'ne karşı bir şikâyette bulunuyor. Riverside yetkilileri şikâyetin alındığını doğruladı ancak yorumdan kaçındı. Riverside Polis Departmanı, Ocak ayında YouTube videosundan sonra soruşturma başlattı ve şimdi ikinci bir mağdurun da gelip başvurduğunu doğruladı. Dedektifler, iki durumu da inceliyor. Ceza hukuku açısından zaman aşımı sorunu olabilir, ancak araştırmacılar kanıtlara dayalı olarak tüm olası suçları araştırıyorlar. Öğretmen, CNN'in telefon ve e-posta isteklerine cevap vermedi. Mağdurların savunucuları, bu davanın öğrencileri daha iyi korumak ve kurumlara sorumluluk yüklemek için yasal reformlara yol açmasını umuyor.

article_content: In a significant development in Somalia’s fight against extremism, Zakariya Ismail Ahmed Hersi, once among the most wanted leaders of al-Shabab, has turned himself in to local police in the Gedo region. The U.S. had placed a $3 million bounty on his head back in 2012 as part of a broader $33 million reward package targeting seven top al-Shabab figures. According to anonymous Somali intelligence sources, Hersi’s decision to surrender may stem from growing tensions within the group after the death of its former leader, Ahmed Abdi Godane—who was eliminated in a U.S. drone strike in 2014. Since then, Hersi had been living in hiding. While Somali officials describe Hersi as a key figure overseeing intelligence and financial operations for the militant group, al-Shabab itself disputes this, claiming he had already left the organization two years before his surrender and never held such a senior position. One Somali military source, Mohamed Osmail, said Hersi was found hiding in a border town and proactively reached out to government contacts to arrange his surrender. Meanwhile, the group’s spokesperson told reporters that Hersi was merely a mid-level commander, not the high-ranking official portrayed by authorities. This contradiction highlights the fog of war surrounding internal al-Shabab dynamics. The surrender comes amid renewed violence: on Christmas Day, al-Shabab attacked an African Union compound in Mogadishu—a site housing the British Embassy and U.N. offices—killing nine people, including three AU troops. The group claimed the raid targeted a Christmas celebration and was retaliation for Godane’s death. While al-Shabab asserted 14 soldiers died, independent assessments suggest inflated casualty figures are common in their statements. Despite losing control of major cities like Mogadishu between 2007 and 2011, al-Shabab still carries out frequent attacks across Somalia and in neighboring Kenya, where AU forces are deployed to support the weak Somali government. The U.S. and U.N. continue to warn that political fragmentation within Somalia threatens hard-won security gains, as the federal government struggles to exert influence beyond the capital.

article_content: A banker, his wife, and their nine-year-old nephew were killed in a drive-by shooting outside their home in Visé, Belgium. Benoit Philippens, a 37-year-old director at BNP Paribas Fortis, was shot along with his wife, Carol Haid, 37—who was also the boy’s godmother—and their nephew as the family arrived at their driveway on Friday. Philippens and the child died at the scene. Carol Haid succumbed to her injuries the following day after being struck three times in the back. Witnesses and judicial sources believe the attackers used an automatic weapon from a passing vehicle, though a bullet hole found in the window of a nearby sports center suggests the shooter may have been positioned near the house. The suspects have not been identified, and no motive has been officially confirmed. Mayor Marcel Neven suggested the attack might be connected to Philippens’ profession. According to reports from L'Événir and 7Dimanche, Philippens had been involved in a public argument with a customer approximately six months earlier, during which he received threats. Neighbors said the couple had been married just over a year and had lived in the home for five or six years. They emphasized that the family was ordinary and had no known ties to drugs or criminal activity.

article_content: By Alex Hawkes. Published: 17:00 EST, 23 March 2013. Updated: 17:00 EST, 23 March 2013. Sir Joshua Reynolds’ portrait of Omai was exempt from capital gains tax because it was used in the business of opening the house to the public. Following a landmark ruling, owners of multi-million-pound artworks may now classify their paintings as 'wasting assets' to avoid hefty capital gains tax (CGT) bills. The Howard family successfully argued that their £9.4 million portrait by 18th-century English painter Sir Joshua Reynolds qualified as 'plant and machinery' at their stately home — and thus, a 'wasting asset' exempt from CGT. They claimed the painting, depicting Omai — a South Sea Islander who spent two years in England in the 1770s after being brought to Britain by Captain Cook’s ship HMS Adventure — was displayed to attract visitors, thereby declining in value for tax purposes. Wealthy aristocrats, nightclub owners, and high-end restaurant operators are now considering similar strategies to shield valuable collectibles from CGT. Sold at Sotheby’s in 2001, the painting had been on public display for decades at the Howards’ Yorkshire estate — famously used as a filming location for ITV’s 1981 adaptation of Brideshead Revisited. In a recent Upper Tribunal judgment, Mr Justice Morgan accepted that although it seemed counterintuitive to treat a high-value, long-lasting painting as a wasting asset, it met the established legal test. HM Revenue & Customs warned the ruling could open a major tax avoidance loophole, but the court upheld the exemption. Tax advisers, including Mike Warburton of Grant Thornton, say the decision has broad implications: 'If you hang a Jimi Hendrix guitar on the wall of your nightclub for ambiance, it could qualify as plant,' he said. Individuals typically pay up to 28% CGT on gains from selling valuable items. It remains unclear how much the Howard family avoided, but the painting was originally acquired by Frederick Howard, the 5th Earl of Carlisle, in the 1790s. Mr. Warburton noted the ruling exposes confusion in tax law: 'A valuable painting will likely last over 50 years and increase in value — few would call it 'plant.' Yet legally, it was classified as such.' A spokesperson for the Howard family confirmed: 'For many years, the painting was on display to visitors. The judge ruled Omai was 'plant' used in the business of opening the house to the public — qualifying it for CGT exemption upon sale.'

Howard ailesi, 18. yüzyıl İngiliz ressamı Sir Joshua Reynolds’in 9,4 milyon sterlinlik tablosunun, şatosundaki 'teçhizat ve makine' kapsamında olduğunu ve bu nedenle SKV'den muaf bir 'tükenen varlık' olduğunu başarıyla savundu. article_content: Maria C. Waltherr-Willard, a longtime French and Spanish teacher in Ohio’s Mariemont School District, attempted to sue the district after being moved from teaching high school to middle school students — but her case was ultimately dismissed by federal judges. She claimed to suffer from pedophobia, a deep-seated fear of young children, and argued that the district violated her rights by assigning her to teach younger students despite knowing about her condition. However, court records show that for more than 12 years, the district had actively accommodated her by keeping her exclusively at the high school level, where she taught advanced French and beginner Spanish. The shift came only after the district discontinued in-person French instruction and moved those courses online, eliminating the need for a full-time high school French teacher. At that point, Superintendent Paul Imhoff consulted with Principal James Renner, who disclosed Willard’s long-standing diagnosis. A prior psychiatric evaluation had confirmed she was unable to teach children under 12, making middle school placement a logical, medically-informed adjustment. Surprisingly, Willard didn’t object at first — in fact, she reportedly expressed excitement about the new role when she started in September 2010. Only six months later did she request a return to the high school, citing underutilization of her skills and concerns about her health. When told no positions were available, she retired shortly afterward. Two years after leaving, she filed a lawsuit alleging disability and age discrimination, claiming the transfer triggered severe health issues including spikes in blood pressure. The courts found no merit in her claims: the district had consistently accommodated her needs, her replacement was nearly the same age, and no evidence showed she was mocked or targeted because of her condition. Ultimately, the judge ruled the reassignment was a practical response to curricular changes — not discrimination.

O, genç çocuklardan korktuğunu iddia eden pedofobi adlı bir durumdan muzdarip olduğunu ve ilçenin bu durumunu bilmesine rağmen daha genç öğrencileri öğretmeye zorladığını savundu. Ancak mahkeme kayıtları, ilçenin onun için 12 yıldan fazla süre boyunca sadece lise seviyesinde çalışmasını sağlayarak sürekli olarak uyum sağladığını gösteriyor. Bu değişiklik, ilçenin lisedeki Fransızca derslerini kesip bunları çevrimiçi hale getirmesinin ardından gerçekleşti ve bu da lisede tam zamanlı Fransızca öğretmeni ihtiyacını ortadan kaldırdı. Bu noktada, müdür Paul Imhoff, Willard'ın uzun süredir bilinen tanısından haberdar olan başöğretmen James Renner ile görüştü. Daha önce yapılan bir psikiyatrik değerlendirme, onun 12 yaşın altındaki öğrencileri öğretmekten engellendiğini doğrulamıştı, bu nedenle ortaokula atanması mantıklı ve tıbbi olarak desteklenen bir adım oldu. Şaşırtıcı bir şekilde, Willard ilk başta itiraz etmedi — hatta Eylül 2010'da yeni görevine başlarken bu rolüne heyecanla baktığı bildirildi. Ancak sadece altı ay sonra, yeteneklerinin ortaokulda yetersiz kullanıldığını ve burada bir yıl daha kalmasının 'sağlığına daha fazla zarar vereceğini' söyleyerek liseye geri dönmek istedi. Hiçbir pozisyonun mevcut olmadığı söylendiğinde, kısa bir süre sonra emekli oldu. Ayrılmaktan iki yıl sonra, taşınmanın ciddi sağlık sorunlarına — özellikle kan basıncında artışlara — neden olduğunu iddia ederek engellilik ve yaş ayrımcılığı iddialarıyla dava açtı. Mahkemeler, bu iddiaların hiçbirinin geçerli olmadığını buldu: ilçe onun ihtiyaçlarını sürekli olarak karşılamıştı, yerine geçen kişi neredeyse aynı yaştaydı ve onun yaşına veya pedofobisine yönelik aşağılama veya tacizle ilgili hiçbir kanıt bulunmamıştı. Sonuç olarak, hakim, bu atamanın ayrımcılık değil, müfredat değişikliklerine yönelik pratik bir tepki olduğunu kararlaştırdı.

article_content: The Pacific Island nation of Kiribati may become the first country to vanish beneath rising seas caused by climate change. Its people fear their homeland could turn into the world’s next Atlantis. As our boat approaches the shore, dark shapes beneath the waves resolve into clear outlines: neatly arranged coral stones, gleaming in the shallows of a quiet cove. We are drifting over the submerged ruins of Tebunginako — a village that once housed more than 200 families. Today, it lies buried under several meters of turquoise water. 'We used to swim out there as boys to watch the ships,' says the Mayor, gesturing proudly toward the underwater remains. 'They’d tie their ropes to the coconut trees right over here.' Tebunginako was once Kiribati’s main harbor — until the sea claimed its coastline. Now, the stumps of dead coconut trees rise from the lagoon like tombstones marking a lost civilization. This kind of extreme coastal erosion is becoming tragically common across Kiribati, a string of 33 islands along the equator. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change lists Kiribati among the six Pacific nations most at risk from sea-level rise. According to its reports, due to ongoing erosion and saltwater contamination of freshwater sources, Kiribati could become uninhabitable by 2050. 'We’re now seeing total flooding in areas that never used to be affected by normal tides,' says Andrew Teem, Kiribati’s Senior Adviser on Climate Change. 'We call them King Tides — enormous surges that didn’t exist when I was a child.' Many Kiribati citizens have already been forced to flee their homes. Half the nation’s population now lives on South Tarawa — a narrow sliver of land so densely packed it rivals Tokyo or London in population density. Without intervention, the island’s population could double by 2030. 'Like all developing island nations, we have a very young, rapidly growing population — and our freshwater supply is already stretched thin,' Teem explains. 'Climate change isn’t creating a new crisis. It’s worsening one we’ve always struggled with.' This week, representatives from 190 countries are meeting in Lima, Peru, for the 20th U.N. Climate Change Conference. Their goal: lay the foundation for a global climate treaty by the end of 2015, to take effect by 2020. But for Kiribati, these deadlines feel dangerously distant. For communities like Tebunginako, the time for action passed years ago. 'Climate change isn’t a future threat for us — it’s happening right now,' Teem insists. 'For other nations, it’s a forecast. For us, it’s our daily reality.' Over the past decade, Kiribati has pursued multiple adaptation strategies: labor migration programs with Australia and New Zealand, and even plans for artificial floating islands. This year, it purchased land in Fiji — a potential refuge for future generations. Yet the people refuse to leave without a fight. Beyond adaptation, they demand justice: binding global carbon cuts and reparations from the nations most responsible for emissions. Recent breakthroughs — including pledges by the U.S. and China to reduce emissions over the next 20 years, and billions pledged by G20 nations to the U.N.’s Green Climate Fund — are welcome, but deemed inadequate. 'These measures are a drop in the ocean,' environmental advocates say. And Teem echoes the sentiment: 'We didn’t cause this. If we had, we’d accept the consequences. But we’re simple people with simple needs — and we shouldn’t be paying for someone else’s excess.' As the sun sets over Tebunginako, the Mayor leads us to the last standing structures: a church and a maneaba — the traditional communal hall. Both rise defiantly from the lagoon, held together by leaky sandbags and crumbling seawalls. 'We keep them alive as reminders,' he says softly. 'They’re sacred. They’re where our people gathered — the last place we were all together.' When asked about the future, he looks to the past. 'We are afraid. We need help. We trust our government to speak for us — but we’re still waiting for the world to answer.' He pauses, staring at the water. 'We used to swim out there... and tie the boats to the coconut trees.'
translated_content: Pasifik adası ülkesi Kiribati, iklim değişikliğinden kaynaklanan yükselen deniz seviyeleri altında kaybolacak ilk ülke olabilir. İnsanları, ana yurdu dünyanın bir sonraki Atlantis’i olabileceğinden korkuyor. Teknemiz kıyıya yaklaştıkça, denizin altındaki koyu gölgeler netleşiyor: düzenli sıralar halinde dizilmiş mercan taşları, sığ bir koyun resifinde parlıyor. Biz, Tebunginako’nun teslim edilmiş mahallelerinin temellerinin üzerinde süzülüyoruz. Köy, bir zamanlar 200’den fazla aileye ev sahipliği yapıyordu, ancak bugün, birkaç metre turkuaz su altında kalıyor. 'Çocukken oraya yüzerek gemileri izlerdik. Gemileri tam buradaki Hindistan cevizi ağaçlarına bağlardı,' diyor Belediye Başkanı, kasabanın kalıntılarının üzerinden geçerken heyecanla işaret ediyor. Tebunginako, bir zamanlar Kiribati’nin ana limanıydı — yükselen deniz kıyısını yuttuğunda. Şimdi ölü Hindistan cevizi ağaçlarının direkleri lagüne uzanıyor, suyun üstünde kafaları küçük mezar taşları gibi beliriyor. Tebunginako’nun aşırı kıyı erozyonu, ekvator boyunca uzanan 33 adadan oluşan Güney Pasifik ülkesi Kiribati’de giderek daha yaygın hale geliyor. Hükümetlerarası İklim Değişikliği Paneli, Kiribati’yi yükselen deniz seviyeleriyle en çok tehdit altındaki altı Pasifik adası ülkesinden biri olarak tanımlıyor. Rapor, kıyı erozyonu ve tatlı su kirlenmesi nedeniyle Kiribati’nin 2050 yılına kadar yaşanmaz hale gelebileceğini iddia ediyor. 'Şu anda, daha önce normal gelgitlerden etkilenmeyen alanların tamamen su altında kaldığını yaşıyoruz,' diyor Kiribati’nin İklim Değişikliği Üst Danışmanı Andrew Teem. 'Bana çocukken bilinmeyen, 'Kral Gelgitleri' adı verilen çok yüksek gelgitler yaşıyoruz.' Kiribati’nin büyük bir kısmı, iklimle ilgili felaketler nedeniyle zaten iç göç etmiş ve birçok kişi başkent adası Güney Tarawa’ya kaçmış durumda. Bugün, Kiribati’nin nüfusunun yarısı, Tokyo veya Londra’nın nüfus yoğunluğunu yansıtan, küçük bir ay şeklindeki Güney Tarawa’ya sığıyor. Doğum oranları veya iç göç kontrol edilmezse, Güney Tarawa’nın nüfusu 2030 yılına kadar ikiye katlanacak. 'Her gelişmekte olan ada devleti gibi, nüfusumuz oldukça genç ve çok hızlı bir şekilde büyüyor, bu da zaten tatlı su arzımızı zorluyor,' diyor Teem. 'İklim değişikliği ve yükselen deniz, zaten sahip olduğumuz su kaynakları sorununu ağırlaştırıyor.' Bu hafta, 190 ülkenin temsilcileri, 2020 yılında uygulanmak üzere 2015 yılının sonunda bir iklim anlaşması hazırlamak amacıyla Peru’nun Lima şehrinde Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Konferansının 20. oturumuna katılıyor. Ancak Kiribati gibi düşük yükseklikteki ada ülkeleri için bu taahhütler yeterince hızlı gelmeyebilir. Tebunginako gibi topluluklar için bu anlaşmalar zaten çok geç. 'İklim değişikliği, diğer bazı ülkeler gibi gelecekte değil, bugün bizim halkımız için büyük sonuçlara sahip,' diyor Teem. 'Diğer ülkeler için bir tahmin. Bizim için günlük gerçeklik.' Son on yılda Kiribati, çeşitli uyum girişimlerinde bulundu: Avustralya ve Yeni Zelanda ile istihdamla ilişkili göç programları ve yapay dalgalı adaların keşfi gibi. Bu yıl, gelecekte kullanmak umuduyla Fijide bir arazi satın aldı. Ancak halk, mücadelesiz evlerini terk etmeye razı değil. Yerel çabalarının yanı sıra, küresel karbon emisyonları gibi sorunun kökenini uluslararası düzeyde zorluyorlar. Kiribati hükümeti, diğer küçük ada devletleriyle birlikte, bağlayıcı karbon emisyonu anlaşmaları için lobi faaliyetlerinde bulunuyor. Ayrıca, endüstriyel güçlerin neden olduğu iklimle ilgili hasarlar için endüstriyel olmayan gelişmekte olan ülkeleri karşılamak üzere 'iklim değişikliği tazminatları' kavramını destekliyorlar. Geçen ay, her iki alanda da atılımlar sağlandı. Dünyanın en büyük karbon emiterleri olan ABD ve Çin, önümüzdeki yirmi yıl içinde emisyonlarını azaltma planlarını duyurdu. Son G20 konferansında, birkaç ülke, Birleşmiş Milletler Yeşil İklim Fonu’na milyarlarca dolar bağışlamak için Başkan Obama ile birlikte taahhütte bulundu; bu fon, gelişmekte olan ülkelerin iklim değişikliğinin etkileriyle mücadele etmesine yardımcı olacak. Kiribati hükümeti bu haberi memnuniyetle karşılasa da, bu önlemler ulusal ihtiyaçlarını karşılamak için yalnızca bir ilk adım. Çevre grupları bu gelişmeleri 'okyanusta bir damla' olarak eleştiriyor. 'İklim değişikliği, bizim sorumluluğumuzda olmayan bir şey,' diyor Teem, iklim değişikliği tazminatları ve karbon emisyonu kesimleri konularında. 'Bu kaderden sorumlu olsaydık, hikâye tamamen farklı olurdu. Biz çok basit insanlar, çok basit ihtiyaçlara sahibiz — ama kendi yapmadığımız bir şeye karşı ödeme yapmak zorunda kalmak istemiyoruz.' Tebunginako’da güneş battığında, Belediye Başkanı bizi kasabanın iki kalan yapısına, bir kiliseye ve geleneksel topluluk merkezi olan maneaba’ya götürür. Yüksek yapılar, lagünün ortasından cesaretle yükseliyor, sadece sızan kum çantalarıyla ve hasar görmüş kıyı koruma duvarlarıyla destekleniyor. 'Onları, Tebunginako’nun hatırına saklı tutmak için mücadele ediyoruz,' diyor Belediye Başkanı. 'Bu yerler, dinimizden dolayı ve hepimizin birlikte olduğu son yer olduğu için halkımız için önemlidir.' Gelecekleri hakkında sorulduğunda, geçmişe sarılıyor. 'Çok korkuyoruz ve yardıma ihtiyacımız var,' diyor. 'Hükümetimize ve dünyaya güçlü seslerini taşıma konusundaki inancımıza güveniyoruz, ancak hala dünyanın cevap vermesini bekliyoruz.' Gözleri suya boş bir şekilde dönerek, hafifçe tekrar ediyor: 'Çocukken oraya yüzerdik… ve gemileri Hindistan cevizi ağaçlarına bağlardık…'
